utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Smith: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we begin today, I'd just like to ask you to listen carefully to the question and just answer the particular question that's being asked. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you mentioned that you were beaten before you were taken to the KP Dom and then, the day after you arrived, you were interviewed by a Boro Ivanovic and a person by the name of Milorad. Also you --

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also you stated that when you arrived at the KP Dom, that you were met by a -- initially you said a Risto Vukovic and later you said a Risto Ivanovic. Who met you from the KP Dom when you first arrived? Was it Vukovic or Ivanovic or was it both people?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Risto Ivanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned yesterday that when you were interviewed that one of the four people - sorry, interrogated - one of the four people in the room slapped you. Who was that? Was that Boro, Milorad, or one of the other two soldiers - sorry - other two people that you could not name?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one of those two other people whose names I don't know, one of them slapped me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned that a person by the Milorad [sic] was in the room. You didn't know his surname, but I'm just going to ask you a few questions about him now. How old was Milorad?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 55 years old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anything particular about his hair that you could describe?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had sideburns. I couldn't see anything else because I was in shock. So when I came in, I looked around and I only saw his sideburns and nothing else, because I was in shock when I came -- when I came and I saw the troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean you cannot remember anything else about his description?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether this person was carrying anything?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had some kind of a bag.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what type of bag was that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A yellowish leather one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see this Milorad in the KP Dom again whilst you were there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen this Milorad that was involved in the interrogation since that time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you think that you would be able to recognise this person if you ever saw him again?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's one last question I'd just like to clear up. Do you know what he was wearing, what clothes?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this first interview, interrogation, were you taken back to your isolation cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For about how long were you kept in this same isolation cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after being in this cell for about three months, where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After three months, I was given a bath first and then I was taken to another isolation cell and I remained there until the end in that cell, isolation cell.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please come closer to the microphone? We have trouble hearing him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sir, would you move your chair closer to the microphone so that your voice is clearer for the interpreters. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For about how long did you spend in this second isolation cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I left in late May, to Cajnice. I was exchanged in Cajnice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you taken in Cajnice?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the police station, SUP building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long were you kept at the police station?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They kept me in SUP for a month, and then after a month, I was exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What month were you exchanged in 1992?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: July 7th, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, that was my mistake, 1993. You mentioned that you were taken to a second isolation cell after about three months. Was that on the same ground floor as the one that you were on, or was it upstairs?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was upstairs, and then there we had beds. We also had bed linen. And I stayed there for about a month. And from that isolation cell, I would go to the kitchen to eat, and after eating, I would be taken back to the isolation cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was that second place that you were taken to, that second isolation cell, was that larger or the same size as the first one that you were taken to and spent three months in?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Larger, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd now like to go back to the topic of interrogations at the KP Dom. After the first interrogation that you had with this Boro Ivanovic and Milorad, were you ever interrogated again?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milorad didn't interrogate me. Only Boro did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this first interrogation, about how many other interrogations were there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 15 interrogations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Boro conduct every one of these?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were these interrogations conducted? Were they conducted in the same place or a different place than your first one?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Same place, where I was brought in the first day, the first evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know which building that was in at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was the first gate and then the second gate, and right there at the entrance, towards the right, towards right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did this building have a name?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said that Milorad wasn't present at these other interrogations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember what Boro Ivanovic was wearing when you were being questioned?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had a camouflage uniform on him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what questions did he ask you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked me about military positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During any of these questionings, were you ever told why you were detained at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you beaten at all during any of these other interrogations?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm referring to these other interrogations with Boro Ivanovic, after the first one.

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand your question. Do you mean when I was in the isolation cells or while I was interrogated?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just mean whilst you were interrogated by Boro Ivanovic; after the first interrogation, were you ever beaten by him or anyone else in the room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you some questions about the solitary confinement cell that you were kept in for that first three months. What was the size of the cell in metres?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately three and a half metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that three and a half metres square?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't tell you exactly. There were three of us laying there, so -- and we couldn't fit there. I can't tell you exactly what the size was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the floor surface in that cell, what was the surface of the floor?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no floor, only concrete there, and we had a sponge of about four centimetres and a blanket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any beds in this room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Smith, he refers there to a sponge. I think he Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. means there a mattress, but you had better clear it up.

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how to explain this, but it was a sponge, four centimetres thick, and I slept on it. And I lived there for three months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this sponge a very, very thin mattress?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very thin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from this sponge or thin mattress, was there any other furniture in the room, like a bed or anything else?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What else was in this cell? Was there a toilet?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that cell there was a toilet and a faucet, water faucet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that certainly at one stage there were three of you in the cell. Did all three of you have a sponge mattress to sleep on or was it just the one sponge mattress?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how can I tell you? We had three sponge mattresses, and when we would leave isolation cells, we would all take our sponge mattresses with us. We spent a night there, several nights, and it was -- the space was quite limited in that cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the cell door locked?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to leave the cell during the day or night?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you allowed out for any sort of physical exercise?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about this cell that you were kept in for about three months. During that time, during that first three months, were you allowed out for meals?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question? I didn't understand it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this first cell that you were placed in and kept in for three months, were you allowed out for meals or were meals delivered to your cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The meals were brought into the cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who brought these meals to the cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whilst you were in the cell, were you given any reading or writing material?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you given anything to occupy your mind during the day and night?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about physical exercise within the cell? Were you given anything to exercise with?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What would you do in the cell during these three months?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had a small sponge and I would dust the room or just clean around the room, and that's what I did for three months. I would simply clean so that the time would go faster. The conditions were bad, food was bad. I had constipation for 29 days and then I had diarrhoea for four days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at the KP Dom, how much did you weigh? Sorry. I don't think I was heard there. When you arrived at the KP Dom, how much did you weigh?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seventy-six kilograms, and from there I went down to forty-six kilograms, so you can imagine what kind of food we had there. When I came home, my own child couldn't recognise me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did your child recognise you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I smiled, then my child said, "Well, this is my father. Here's my father."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at the Cajnice police station and you were kept there for about a month, was the food better or worse than at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The food was good in Cajnice. It was very good. There's nothing else I can add.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you'd like to have a drink, have a glass of water, would you like to do that? In the cell, were there any windows?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please repeat the question? Do you mean in Cajnice or in Foca?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the cell, the first cell that you were in for that three months in Foca.

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Foca, during the first three months, there was a window but quite high, so I couldn't see what was going on there. The lights were on only in the hallway. There were no lights in the isolation cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the windows on the hallway side of the cell or opposite that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The windows were on side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At nighttime, was there any light coming into the cell from outside? You said there was no lighting in the cell, but was there any lighting coming from outside?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the day, did this cell get any lighter?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, somewhat lighter, not much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it light enough to read, if you could?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that three months in isolation, did you ever see the sun?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that when you first arrived at the KP Dom and were placed in the cell, there was no heating. Was any heating placed in this cell over that three-month period that you were there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned there was a window in the cell. Was that open or shut?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Open.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to shut it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why not? Why couldn't you shut it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was high, so I couldn't close it. I had nothing to climb on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe how cold the room was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that room was very cold. It was February, so it was definitely below zero. It was quite cold, and this is where my hearing deteriorated. And prior to that, when I'd been beaten, the situation got worse and now I can hardly hear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the tap water in that cell ever freeze whilst you were there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did it freeze for?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seven days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you provided water by someone else during that seven-day period?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any hot water in this cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any basin or cup or some sort of water holder in which you could pour water into?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that when you arrived at the KP Dom on the first night, you weren't given a change of clothes. For the time that you were in the cell for that three-month period, were you ever given a change of clothes?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sleep in the same clothes that you wore during the day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the prison authorities ever offer to wash your clothes? Did anyone come in and say, "We will wash your clothes"?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to wash your clothes in the cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the three months that you were there, were you given any hygiene products at all, like soap, toilet paper, toothpaste, shampoo?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever have a shower or a bath while you were in that cell for that three months?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from the times that you were interviewed by Boro Ivanovic, did you ever leave that cell during that three-month period?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Red Cross ever visit you whilst you were in that cell for three months?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you able to contact any family, friends or other officials?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of these people contact you whilst you were at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For most of the time that you were in this cell for this three-month period, were you by yourself or were you sharing it with other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, during the first month, I was practically alone in the isolation cell; and during this second month these colleagues from the neighbouring isolation cell, when actually some of their colleagues would get drunk, then they would bring Karisik Adil and Ljubo to sleep with me in this isolation cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what Ljubo's full name is?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat this question? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that an Adil and a Ljubo would come into your cell occasionally. Do you know what Ljubo's full name is?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Durmisevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think you also mentioned that they came into your cell when some of their colleagues would get drunk. When you mean "their colleagues," who do you mean? Colleagues of the people that were working at the KP Dom or someone else?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I imagine when their soldiers get drunk and don't want to go out to the front line to fight, then they lock them up in isolation cells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you mean Serb or Muslim soldiers, or do you not know?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did this Adil and Ljubo come into your cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they would come like every 15 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how often would they stay? How often would they stay in your cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it all depended on the kind of punishment that was meted out. They would spend five or six days with me and then they would be taken back to their isolation cells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "punishment that would be meted out," do you mean punishment meted out to Adil and Ljubo or punishment meted out to these Serb soldiers that wouldn't go to the front line?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serb soldiers were punished, those who did not want to go to the front line, and that's why they locked them up and that's why they locked more of us up into the same isolation cell. They would punish them for about five or six days, and then, when this punishment was over, then again they would send us to various isolation cells where we had been before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old was Adil, approximately?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 75 years old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did he come from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Strgacine, near Rudo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why he was arrested?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how old was this person called Ljubo?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was also 75, if not even more. He wasn't any younger than that, not younger.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was he from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were these two men, were they in any form of military unit?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that they slept in your cell occasionally for five to six days at a time. Was there enough room for you all to sleep on the floor?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to sleep, then?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we slept next to one another. We couldn't sleep on the back, so we would have to sleep on the side, all of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice anything about Ljubo when you first saw him, about his health?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you notice?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I noticed that his ear had been cut open to a blood vessel, and he asked for first aid, but nobody came to help him and to clean that wound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long was the cut?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't say exactly, but all the way to the blood vessel. You know where the blood vessel is in the ear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it a deep cut or was it just a minor cut?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was deep. Part of the ear was up and the other part was down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe how long this cut was in centimetres or inches?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. I didn't measure it. But try to understand this. Try to understand what I said. One part went up and the other part went down. They wanted them to sew his ear together, you see. When I saw this, he asked me, "What should I do? This ear keeps hanging. The other side is up."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he ever given a bandage for this wound?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At one stage was Edib (sic) and Ljubo taken out of solitary confinement?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe what happened when they were taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can describe it. It was lunchtime, sometime around 3.00. A soldier came and read this name out. Ejub was with me then. He said: Durmisevic Edib (sic) and -- Durmisevic and Fatima, some Fatima. She was not there with us. I don't know. And then he went up to Adil and then he came back to my place. And he said, "Did you get ready, old man?" And he said "Yes." And Ejub kissed me and he said, "If I go to Sarajevo or to Kalinovik, I'll try to rescue you."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Ejub Ljubo?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question. What do you mean by "Ljubo"? You mean Adil, do you? Ejub; it's not Ljubo but Ejub.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Ejub Durmisevic, was he in your cell when he was taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Adil in your cell at that time or was he in some other place?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was in his cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that cell next to yours?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just would like to clear something up. A moment ago you talked about a Ljubo Durmisevic being in your cell and then you referred to an Ejub Durmisevic. Is Ejub and Ljubo the same name? Is Ljubo a nickname for Ejub?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not Ljubo. Maybe I made a mistake. It was Ejub who was with me, not Ljubo. Ejub was in the same room with me. And then when this soldier opened this isolation cell, he said -- he said, "Durmisevic Ejub, get ready." And then he went to Adil's isolation cell, called out his name, and then he came back to get Ejub, and then they closed the door and left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned a woman by the name of Fatima. Did you see her at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you hear that she was taken out with these two on that day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know Fatima was being called out at the same time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when he read Ejub's and Adil's name, he also read Fatima's name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you didn't know of a Fatima being at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since that day that they were taken out, have you ever seen them again?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know of anyone that has seen either of these two men alive since then?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After these two men were taken out of the isolation cells, did you meet any other men who were detained in these cells?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who were they?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two more men, Starhonic Hasan, and Masic Elvedin.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters have difficulty hearing the witness. His microphone seems to be off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Can we check that, please? Ask another question, Mr. Smith. Ask another question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that after these two people left, you met an Elvedin and a Hasan. Is it Elvedin Masic and Hasan Starhonic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Was it working that time?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I think it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Elvedin Masic, about how old was he?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was born in 1975 or something like that. Believe me, I didn't ask him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Hasan Starhonic, about how old was he?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he's somewhere around there, too. To tell you the truth, I didn't ask him either but they were roughly the same age. I was the oldest of the three of us. I was older than the two of them, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about how long did they stay in solitary confinement?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They stayed with me until I left. Then they took us out of there. It was the end of April. They took us to a different isolation cell. They let us have a bath, and then, towards the end of May, we were taken to Cajnice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whilst you were in the isolation cells, did you meet a Dzevad Cosovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did not meet him. He was locked up in the isolation cell next door to mine, and I actually had contact with him through the wall, asked him, like, "Where are you from," and things like that, but I didn't have any direct contact with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why he was placed in the isolation cell? Did he tell you? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember how long he was placed there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately for seven days.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, this person is referred to in Schedule number A -- Schedule A, number 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'd now like to show you a piece of paper. The paper has a name on it and a number. And I would ask you to tell the court whether you met that person or knew that person whilst you were in the isolation cells. Please don't say his name.

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this person --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just one moment. Is there any problem with mentioning his pseudonym, to have it in the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: No. I was just about to. His pseudonym wasn't placed on his original sheet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I realise that, but we have that as one of the pseudonyms in this case. It was FWS-08.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that person you just referred to on that sheet was given the number 8 on that sheet, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. I mean, I did not see this, but this person was mentioned, actually. This person went out to work and that person was locked up in an isolation cell, and I heard this person being beaten. But it's not that I saw this person. Actually, they only mentioned this person's last name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Don't mention his name. But this is the person that was referred to in the sheet with the number 8; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I don't know why you're asking that question. We have all agreed that that is the name on the sheet and that he is identified as FWS-08. Is there any point in keeping on asking this same question?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: No, you're quite correct, Your Honour. There is no --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you heard this person being beaten. Did you actually hear the beating or did you hear through someone else that he was being beaten?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. This man was taken out to work. They say that he also had a brother, and they were quarrelling and fighting or something like that. (redacted).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you -- don't mention this person's name --

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And I'll just ask that it be redacted, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please don't mention this person's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. It seemed to me that the witness said that that person was deaf. However, this was not in the transcript, so could my colleague, the Prosecutor, please check this with the witness? I think he mentioned this, but I can't see it in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Where do you suggest that it was said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is what was said in front of the isolation cell.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 20, line 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I see. Well, Mr. Smith, that's still on the page. You had better follow that up if you think that it's relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This man that was taken out to work, was he deaf?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever meet him whilst you were in the isolation cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did someone tell you he was beaten or did you hear the actual beating yourself?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I heard screams, screams from where he was being beaten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he being beaten in an isolation cell near yours or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, further away from my cell. I only heard the screaming, but I didn't hear in -- I didn't hear which cell it was coming from. That was across.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know who was beating him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how long this person was in the isolation cells whilst you were there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, this person is referred to as A-9 in the schedules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, whilst you were in solitary confinement, were you ever beaten?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who beat you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serb soldiers beat me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many times were you beaten?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately ten times. I was taken out to the hallway, and there they hit me, kicked me in my chin, and threw a patent knife on me and cut my jacket. And I was so scared that I ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were so scared that what?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't tell you what happened to me. I was mortified with fear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you so scared that you defecated in your pants? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this happened on one occasion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That happened on several occasions. I was beaten every five days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember or do you know the name of anyone that beat you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is that person's name?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zoran Matovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he involved in the beatings on every occasion, every one of these ten occasions, or only a few of them?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He beat you on every occasion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that some Serb soldiers were involved in the beating -- involved in the beatings. Was that on every occasion that Zoran Matovic and someone else was involved?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Zoran Matovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the incident when Zoran Matovic beat you and a patent -- and a knife was used?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can describe. He brought in his colleague to ask -- to ask who remained on our side and whether they were still alive. I replied -- well, I didn't know what to tell him, and he started throwing a knife at me and kicked me with his boot on my chin. And I told him, "Can I just go to the bathroom, sir?" And he said, "Yes." And when I came back, he kept asking me, and I told him, "Well, you have a knife, you have a pistol, you have a gun." And then that person who kept questioning me went out and I went back to the isolation cell.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please come closer to the microphone. The interpreters have trouble hearing him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You have moved away from the microphone again, sir. Would you bring your chair up closer and lean forward into it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who kicked you on the chin? Was it Zoran Matovic or this other person?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zoran Matovic. This other person was standing with his cap low on his head and I couldn't recognise him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that this kick caused a cut on your chin. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that cut leave a scar?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show the scar to the Court?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness indicates with his hand to the front of his chin a small scar, perhaps one centimetre in length.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anyone else in the cell whilst you were being beaten on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ejub Durmisevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was he doing whilst this was happening?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was seated on a sponge on which we slept, and when I came in, the cell was open and he just looked at me to see what I looked like, and I just put my arms in the air.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that he threw a knife at you. Did the knife hit you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That knife cut my jacket to pieces but did not hit me. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "cut your jacket to pieces," did it make one cut in your jacket or a number of cuts?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he saying to you when you were being kicked and the knife thrown at you, Zoran Matovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me, "Balija, I'm going to take your heart out with a knife. I'm going to take your heart out." So I was so scared -- I went through so much that I can't even talk about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on this occasion, about how many times were you hit? You said you were kicked. Were you hit any further times than that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this beating, about how many times were you hit?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Twice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that Zoran Matovic beat you about ten times. On these other occasions what would he do to you? How would he beat you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he beat me with his feet, hands, every three days, every five days. I don't want to go into this any further. I simply -- I was so scared that I ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just have to ask a few more questions about this. On these other occasions when you were beaten, was it in the cell or out the front of the cell or some other place?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was both in the cell and in front of the cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what parts of the body were you hit and kicked?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kidneys, spine, head. He hit me around my heart so that I have serious injuries around my heart; kidneys, spine. Well, that's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were these beatings during the day or the night or both?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They beat me during the day and in the evening hours, before dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "they" beat you, you mentioned Zoran Matovic. Were other people involved in the beatings on these other occasions?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you resist these beatings? Did you try and stop him from hitting you when he started?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why didn't you try and resist?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I knew what would ensue if I tried to resist. Then he would bring in help, and I knew what would ensue in that case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Zoran Matovic before you arrived at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you know that this person that was beating you on these ten occasions was, in fact, Zoran Matovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that he locked up his colleague that evening, when I was brought in. Well, approximately five nights after that, when he locked up this colleague of his, I guess that colleague was drunk, and he was kicking the door all night, saying, "Zoran Matovic, fuck your mother, when you lock me up as an Ustasha in this cell." And that's when I heard of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just one moment, the word "Ustasha" was the translation given. It may be a translation, but it won't help me understand what was the sense of the word used. It doesn't appear in the transcript. It's got a hat on it, which means a subsequent query, but my hearing of it was Ustasha.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you mention the word "Ustasha" a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who said this word, the Ustasha? Was it the Serb prisoner that was being locked up?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Serb prisoner that was locked up there that night, he kicked the door the entire night. He was very drunk, I guess, and I guess he was upset that he was locked up there, and he mentioned his last name then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what does the -- what does "Ustasha" mean? What does the word mean?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could I know?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Zoran Matovic on shift that night?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I guess he was, since he mentioned him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 23rd of September, 1994, you made a statement to the Gorazde police, the Serb security services there, and you said that the person that kicked and attacked you with a knife was a person by the name of Zoran Pljevaljcic. And you don't mention Zoran Matovic in the statement. Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that statement was given shortly after, and I didn't really have time to look it over, and it wasn't correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a person with the name Zoran Pljevaljcic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also in that statement, you refer to the incident of the knife and being kicked, but you don't refer to the further incidents relating to the other beatings by Zoran Matovic. Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that first statement that you gave to the officials in 1994, you mentioned being assaulted with a knife and being kicked in the chin, but you didn't mention the other beatings that you received from Zoran Matovic. Can you explain why it doesn't appear in the first statement?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that statement was given shortly afterwards as well, so I didn't have time to give it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give a brief description of Zoran Matovic? Was he younger or older than you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think he was younger than me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember what he wore?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember anything further about him, the colour of his hair or how tall he was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whilst you were at KP Dom, did you know who the managers of the prison were?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why is that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because nobody told me. Well, because I don't know who the warden of the KP Dom was except on that day when I was questioned by this Milorad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't know that this Milorad was the warden of the KP Dom at that time, did you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand this question. "You didn't know that this Milorad was the warden of the KP Dom at that time?" When did the witness state that Milorad was the warden? The Prosecutor asked in detail whether he -- the witness could describe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The objection is a valid one because your question assumes that he had said it at an earlier stage, and he hasn't. He said he didn't know who Milorad was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, and that's an assumption that I didn't want to impart within that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I realise that it might have been a badly-worded question, but, nevertheless, Mr. Bakrac's point is a good one. So that question is rejected. You'd better try it again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the day that you were questioned, did you know who the warden of the KP Dom was? This is the day that you were questioned after you arrived at the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The day -- that day when I was interrogated, I knew only then, when I was interrogated, Boro said, "Milorad, write this down." And I never saw Milorad again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, did you know who the warden of the KP Dom was? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After three months in the isolation cell, you said that you were transferred to another cell, which was bigger than the one that you were in.

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned that was the first time, I think, that you were given a bath.

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long -- I think you stated that you stayed in this next room for at least a month. Who else was in that room with you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that room, there was Hasan Starhonic and Elvedin Masic. We were there together. We took a bath together, and then we left that room to go to eat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know the room number of this place that you stayed in after the isolation cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know whether it was on the ground floor or an upper floor?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was upstairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after a month, you've stated that you were taken to Cajnice police station.

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who were you taken with? Which other prisoners? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was Hasan Starhonic, and from there, we were taken to Aladza, up there, and then from the female part of the prison, they took four women and children and took us to Cajnice, and there was another woman and four children waiting for us there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was this female prison? Was it at Velecevo?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know the name of this woman and the children that were picked up from Velecevo?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who took you to the Cajnice police station?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Serb troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Boro Ivanovic involved in this exchange at all, or this transfer to the Cajnice police station?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was his involvement? What did you see?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I saw -- when we were taken to the gate, they told us to empty our pockets because we were going to Cajnice to be exchanged. Boro was there, and another two men, and then we were put on a van, and then there were three of us in the van, and we were brought to Dragocava where there was this female camp, and this is how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say, "this female camp," is this the female prison you were referring to, or some other place?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said, I think, that a woman and her four children were picked up and then you were all taken to Cajnice.

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you stated earlier that you stayed at the Cajnice police station for about one month.

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you exchanged after the one month at the police station?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was exchanged at Ustipraca. I went through Rude, Visegrad, and I was exchanged at Ustipraca, near the tunnel leading towards Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Boro Ivanovic at the Cajnice police station or did you know whether he was involved in your exchange?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he took me to Cajnice and there he left me. He went back to Foca, and I remained there in Cajnice for a month. And then people from Cajnice took me to be exchanged and, in fact, it wasn't Boro who took me to be exchanged. There was other people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we can just go back a moment, you said that when you were taken for transfer from the KP Dom to Cajnice, you met Boro Ivanovic on the way out. Who took you from your room in the KP Dom to the -- to where you met Boro Ivanovic on the way out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I was taken by a soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know the name of that soldier?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd now like to talk about --

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Perhaps, Your Honour -- this is the last topic. It's just in relation to his health. Do you still wish to continue over the next few minutes? It will take about 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We'll give you a few minutes extra. We'll resume at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, before we move on to questions relating to your health, whilst you were at the KP Dom, you said that you didn't know who the management of the KP Dom was. However, did you know a person with the title of Vaspitac?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd now like to ask you some questions about your health condition, and the effects, the physical and psychological effects that the beatings had on you, and I'm referring to the beatings that you received on your arrest and the beatings that you received whilst you were at the KP Dom, and the physical and mental effects that you may have suffered as a result of the conditions at the KP Dom. I'm going to be now asking you some questions about that topic. Do you understand? Witness, prior to coming to the -- prior to arriving at the KP Dom in 1993, did you have a good back? Was your back healthy or did you have any back complaints?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the beatings you received before you arrived at the KP Dom and the beatings that you received whilst at the KP Dom and the conditions that you endured, did you develop a back complaint?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did that back complaint first develop? When did you start to notice some problems?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came to the KP Dom, 20 days I could not get up. I was in an isolation cell which was like a chimney. I had to hold on to the wall and I had to wait for the soldier to pass by. And then if you didn't manage to get your turn to have lunch or dinner, then they would say, "They don't like our food," and then we would be beaten up badly. So my health condition is really poor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of your back problems, could you sleep whilst you were at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what caused these back problems, in your mind?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, because I was so badly beaten on the back and on my head that in my head I've lost my memory and I've had these mental problems. I start going somewhere and I don't know where I'm going, actually; I don't know why I'm going, where I'm going.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you still have problems with your back today?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When the weather is bad, I can't stand straight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to being arrested and taken to the KP Dom, did you have good or normal hearing?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the state of your hearing now in each ear?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you one thing. I can't hear a thing in one ear. I mean, that membrane, it went bust altogether. Fifty-four point three per cent is the degree to which my hearing has been affected, so then you know how well I can hear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it the case that you only have 54 per cent hearing in one ear and no hearing in the other?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. No. I mean, I don't know. I can't hear a thing on this left ear. As for the right ear, my hearing is very poor. I have to put my ear this way and then I can hear; and if somebody is speaking very softly, I can't hear a thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Smith, the figure 54.3 per cent suggests that that is something he's been told by a doctor. Would it be not better for you to obtain that fact? It's hearsay, but nevertheless it's some evidence which would justify the figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I'll put that to him, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to your hearing, you said that you have only 54 per cent hearing in one ear. Who told you that? Did a doctor tell you that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My doctor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when were you given that diagnosis?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I heard about this when I went for a checkup. He took a picture of my ears and gave me the findings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what year was that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did your hearing problem start to develop? You said you had good or normal hearing when you arrived at the KP Dom, or prior to your arrest. When did these problems -- when did you start to go deaf?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I was at the KP Dom, then I went deaf, and this went on and on until I left the KP Dom. When I left the KP Dom, I tried to go and see doctors. They examined me and they gave me some kind of drops, and then all of a sudden I went completely deaf on the right-hand side. He took a picture of my ear and he said that my left ear was no good, that the membrane had gone bust; and on the other ear, he said, "You can hear a little bit, can't you?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what do you believe to be the cause of the deafness? Was it the beatings before you arrived at the KP Dom, the beatings that you received whilst at the KP Dom, or the conditions that you endured at the KP Dom, or something else? What do you think caused your hearing problems?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. I was beaten up quite badly when I was first apprehended. They beat me, they kicked me, they really hit me bad. And then the conditions at the KP Dom were very bad. It was very cold that first year when I was there and also there was a bad draft. There was no heating. You know what it was like. I don't have to explain all this to you again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd just like you to briefly explain these particular answers to the questions to the Court. It's not necessarily for my benefit. In relation to your hearing, how has that affected your life since you left the KP Dom, your loss of hearing?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it did affect my life. A car can hit me. Also, when I watch television, I can't hear at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at the KP Dom, did you have any form of speech Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. impediment, like a stutter?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you developed one since being detained at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you get nervous, do you have any speech problems?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what those speech problems are?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have bad problems. I get this nervousness in my head, and then my entire organism gets so frightened, it's hard for me to enunciate, because all of this has affected me psychologically, this KP Dom and the fear I felt there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how does this nervousness affect your speech?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Badly. When I get a headache, it's as if I were crazy. I find fault with everyone and I can't stand the sight of anyone at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to arriving at the KP Dom, did you have any chest pains, any problems with your chest?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you develop chest pains whilst you were at the KP Dom or afterwards?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I got these pains around the heart. It drives me crazy when I get these pains around the heart area, in this area here, see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what caused these pains? What do you believe caused them?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when they beat me, they beat me with rifle butts, kicked me with their boots. All of this led to these problems. And I didn't have any problems like that before I came to the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just going back a moment, you said that you developed a nervousness from being at the KP Dom. Did you have this nervousness before you arrived at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what do you believe caused this nervousness, this state of nervousness, to develop?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fear. What can I tell you? Fear. When I was taken prisoner, I felt lost. I was so frightened that I could hardly speak from fear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you've briefly mentioned that your detention at the KP Dom has affected you psychologically. Can you explain in more detail how it's affected your behaviour?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The hygiene was poor, poor sleep, poor food. I don't have to tell you all this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you seeking, or have you sought, any medical treatment for the psychological effects of your detention at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen a psychologist or a psychiatrist about the effects of what happened to you at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since leaving the KP Dom, have you seen a doctor generally about the injuries you received?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how often have you seen a doctor about these injuries?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean at the KP Dom? Or when I got home?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got out of the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please repeat your question. You mean when I got home?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. When you got home.

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. Now I understood your question. I went to see my doctor, Langer [phoen], and he took a picture of my ribs and my lungs, and he realised that my fifth rib was broken, there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And today, I mean this year, over the last year, have you received any medical treatment at all?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every year I go for these medical checkups. I go for a checkup every year. I go for a checkup every six months, every three months. That's what the doctors suggested to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are these physical checkups or psychological checkups?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Physical and psychological health. I'm nervous in the head. I have these problems in my head, bad problems. I told you. I am always nervous and I have this very poor memory. When I set out, I don't know where I'm actually going. My memory is non-existent.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Mr. Vasic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good day, sir. I would like to introduce myself, I'm Miroslav Vasic, attorney at law, Defence counsel for the accused Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us whether you gave a statement to the Centre of Public Security in Gorazde on the 23rd of September, 1994, in Gorazde?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you given a statement to the investigator of the OTP on the 22nd of June, 1996?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Did you read both statements and sign them?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall that in the statement that you gave to the sector of the security service in Gorazde, you stated that when you were first interviewed at the KP Dom, there were two persons who were present, Boro Ivanovic and another person?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you exactly. There were four men there, Boro and Milorad and two other men. I did not know the two other men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you state to the public security station that on that occasion, Boro Ivanovic was present and another policeman who beat you then?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was very fast. I don't know exactly how many statements I gave. I mean, it was so fast.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also state to the investigator of the Office of the Prosecutor on the 22nd of June, 1996, that on the occasion of your first questioning in the KP Dom, Boro Ivanovic was present and that, during the interrogation, he brought in another military policeman, another policeman who beat you? Is that what you stated?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear the question, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just before you read it again, remember that when you are reading, you do speed up and the interpreters were having trouble keeping up with you. So if you're reading something, read it slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement to the investigator of the OTP on the 22nd of June, 1996, did you state -- this is document ID 292. This is paragraph 6 on page 2. "On the next day, after I arrived at the KP Dom, I was interrogated by Boro Ivanovic. I did not know him from before, but he introduced himself by this name and said that he was a police inspector. During the interrogation, he threatened me. He questioned me about Serbs in the BiH army and the TO. Boro Ivanovic brought in another policeman during the interrogation who beat me." Did you say this?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that what happened, then?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the way he put it: "If you won't tell the truth, then I have my own people who cut off ears and heads if you lie."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You said today that you were put in an isolation cell. Can you tell me how long and how wide this isolation cell was, the one that you were first put into?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other one was three and a half metres and -- well, how wide was it? The three men, the three of us who were there could not lie in it. So I did not measure it, but I walked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you said that it was approximately three and a half metres long, can you tell us approximately how wide it was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately, I never measured its width, because I walked along its length. I had this little sponge mattress, and I walked and used my own steps to measure it, and I also cleaned it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. After this isolation cell, you were transferred to another room. Can you tell us where this other room was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This other room was -- I can't tell you exactly where, on which floor, but it was upstairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in which part of the building?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the part facing town, from the ground floor on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many persons were in this room when you were brought in?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this other isolation cell?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I mean this other room.

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were three of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was any other person brought into that room subsequently?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. How big was this room? Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. I did not measure it. And again I tell you I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today you spoke to us about the conditions that prevailed at the KP Dom; that it was cold, that the water froze, that there was no light. Did you say that in your previous statements?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the statement that you gave to the investigator of the OTP on the 22nd of June, 1996, you did not mention any details related to darkness in the cell, in the isolation cell, the freezing of water in the tap, that you heard that Matovic said to you, "Balija, I'm going to cut Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. your heart out." Can you explain why you did not say that in this statement of yours?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that statement, everything went real fast and I didn't give it for a long time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the statement at the security centre was very fast and now you say that also in 1996 the statement you gave to the investigator of the OTP on the 22nd of June, 1996 also went real fast. Did I understand you properly?

utterances.speaker: FWS-159 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood you to say that the Office of the Prosecutor in the security station in Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I asked you about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
